ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: the left side of the attached figure is the Nyquist path in the s plane, along the imaginary axis from -j∞ to +j∞, and closed at infinity with a large semicircle in the right half-plane. The right side of the attached figure is the Nyquist plot in the G(s) plane, with the horizontal axis as Re G and the vertical axis as Im G; the curve is labeled 2K at the positive real axis, labeled -K at the leftmost real intercept on the negative real axis, and approximately reaches +j5.43K and -j5.43K up and down. The direction of the curve in the figure has been marked with arrows, and the key visual information is that the leftmost real-axis intercept of this Nyquist curve is -K. Then reason: the open-loop transfer function is G(s)=10K(s+2)/(s^3+3s^2+10). The open-loop poles are determined by the denominator s^3+3s^2+10=0. Make the Routh table for this polynomial: the s^3 row is 1, 0; the s^2 row is 3, 10; the first term of the s^1 row is (3·0-1·10)/3=-10/3; the s^0 row is 10. The first column is 1, 3, -10/3, 10, and the sign changes are from + to - once and from - to + once, for a total of 2 times, so the number of open-loop poles in the right half-plane is P=2. From the figure it can be known that the Nyquist curve reaches leftmost to -K; when 0<K<1, -K is located to the right of -1, so the illustrated Nyquist curve will not encircle the critical point -1. Therefore the net encirclement number N=0. According to the Nyquist criterion, the number of closed-loop right-half-plane poles is Z=P+N=2.

The first column is 1, 3, -10/3, 10, and the sign changes are from + to - once and from - to + once, for a total of 2 times, so the number of open-loop poles in the right half-plane is P=2. From the figure it can be known that the Nyquist curve reaches leftmost to -K; when 0<K<1, -K is located to the right of -1, so the illustrated Nyquist curve will not encircle the critical point -1. Therefore the net encirclement number N=0. According to the Nyquist criterion, the number of closed-loop right-half-plane poles is Z=P+N=2.
